children: According to JPX, TAIFEX and RTHK, Asian index futures drifted lower in the overnight session after a muted Wall Street close, where the Dow added 0.04% to 50,926.56, the S&P 500 rose 0.19% to 7,666.45 and the Nasdaq edged up 0.04% to 26,871.60, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 1.59% to 12,829.00. The dollar index pushed above 102 to a near 18-month high, 10- and 30-year Treasury yields touched fresh 24-year-plus highs before retreating, spot gold tested $4,200 and New York crude climbed nearly 3%.

Nikkei 225 index futures traded on the Osaka Exchange ended the night session at 68,460, down 550 points, after the cash Nikkei closed Thursday at a roughly six-week high. The December-delivery contract moved between an overnight low of 67,790 and a high of 68,860.

Taiwan's TAIEX futures retreated in the night session, with the near-month October contract settling at 48,475, down 223 points or 0.46%, on volume of 37,554 lots. The cash TAIEX had closed Thursday at a record 48,353.49.

Hong Kong's futures market was closed for the National Day holiday, so there was no Hang Seng futures night session into Friday morning. In overnight ADR trade, HSBC's ADR was converted to HK$150.36, 4.84% below its Hong Kong close, as European financial shares came under pressure; Tencent's ADR equated to HK$423.68 (down 1.70%), Alibaba's U.S. shares to HK$105.38 (down 1.14%) and Meituan's ADR to HK$71.01 (down 0.97%).

title: ASIA NIGHT SESSION | Nikkei Futures Slip 0.8% in Osaka Overnight as TAIEX Futures Ease; Hong Kong Shut for Holiday
